sentence_stem: If I had studied harder at school,
correct_completion: I would be in a better job today.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder at school, I would be in a better job today.
acceptable_variants: I would be earning much more money now.
I would have more options at work today.

options.text: I had a better job last year.
options.why_wrong: This describes a past situation and does not give the imagined present result that the 'if' clause calls for.

options.text: so I am working in a shop now.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a real cause and effect, but the sentence needs a hypothetical result after an unreal past condition.

options.text: I would be in a better job today.

options.why_wrong: This states past actions, but the main clause must describe the imagined present result of the condition.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals (unreal past condition with unreal present result)
explanation: A mixed conditional uses a past perfect in the 'if' clause to talk about an unreal past, and would plus a base verb in the main clause to talk about the present result. The result clause refers to now, not to the past.
translation: Si hubiera estudiado más en la escuela, ahora tendría un trabajo mejor.
